description: Agent Purchases: submit a provider’s public purchase facts as an agent buyer meets them: each fact it discloses (the price, the asset and network, how a quote holds, what counts as delivered, how a call can be rehearsed, the refund route and the terms) with when the buyer meets it (before payment, in the 402 challenge, after payment or not at all) and whether it is stated or only implied, how a call is priced (fixed, per unit, quoted or variable, with whether a quote binds the amount settled, how long it holds and any cap), the rehearsal it offers (dry run, sandbox, simulated response, testnet or none, whether it is free and whether it runs on the paid call’s own interface) and how money moves back (refund endpoint, refund process, automatic, contact-us or none, with its window). The signed report gives each readiness piece (disclosure before payment, price and quote, rehearsal, money back) as ready, implied, missing or unstated, and names every fact shown only after payment or not at all, every quote that does not bind, every uncapped variable price, a missing or paid rehearsal and a missing or contact-only refund route, with the fix for each. Readiness for recovery, payouts and adoption is wever_recovery-readiness-check, wever_payout-readiness-check and wever_adoption-readiness-check, and an anonymous visitor’s view of a whole public layer is wever_public-surface-check. A summary sample is wever_provider-readiness-sample on https://weverlabs.com/mcp-free. Verdict not_ready, implied_readiness, readiness_unverified or ready_for_agent_buyers. POST /api/provider-readiness-check. Reads only the material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, sharing, configuration change or external write. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-purchases-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-purchases/.

disclosure.description: What the provider discloses to a buying agent, fact by fact.

form.description: How it is stated: machine readable, in prose, or only implied.

shown.description: When a buying agent meets it.

where.description: Where the buyer meets it, such as the 402 challenge or an OpenAPI description.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

cap.description: The most one call can cost.

quote_binding.description: The quoted amount is the amount settled.

quote_expiry.description: How long a quote holds, such as 5 minutes.

same_interface.description: The rehearsal runs on the paid call’s own endpoint and schema.

route.description: How money moves back when a paid call fails.

window.description: How long after a call money can move back, such as 7 days.

name: wever_provider-readiness-check
title: Provider readiness check
